paragraphs.text: Buying a used car can save a great deal of money, but it also carries risks. A car that looks clean and shiny may have hidden problems that are expensive to repair.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Before looking at any cars, decide how much you can afford to spend in total. Remember to include insurance, tax and the cost of the first service, which buyers often forget.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: When you view a car, always ask to see its service history. A record of regular maintenance suggests that the previous owner looked after the vehicle, while missing records should make you cautious.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: A test drive is essential. Listen for unusual noises, check that the brakes respond evenly and make sure all the lights and windows work. If possible, drive on both quiet roads and a busy main road.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: If you are not confident about checking a car yourself, pay a mechanic to inspect it. The fee is small compared with the cost of discovering a serious fault after you have bought the car.
paragraphs.label: E

headings.text: Evidence of how the car was treated
Checking the car on the road
